_readme: Copy this file to ~/.config/memory-arbiter/config.json, then edit paths.
Keep per-client identity (MEMORY_ARBITER_CLIENT / AGENT_ID / WORKSPACE) in each MCP client's env block.
The default core is model-free. vec/embedding and semantic_conflict are optional local enhancements.
_update_check_readme: When enabled, a one-shot background check may attach a low-frequency update notice.
Set enabled=false to disable network update checks.
_structured_claim_mode_readme: Deterministic write/edit-time extraction for explicit key/value, table, numeric-unit, and semver claims.
A collision is persisted as pending_llm and returned as action_required=judge_conflict_before_use.
The host LLM submits a snapshot-pinned judgment receipt before using the affected claim.
Judgment records guidance only; it never edits or supersedes either memory.
Set off only as an emergency kill switch. There is no periodic vector conflict scanner fallback.

_readme: Optional local write-time semantic notices. Current backend: local_gguf only.
Setting model_path auto-enables this block unless enabled=false is explicit.
Jobs are async/fail-open and inference is strictly serial (max_concurrency is fixed at 1).
job_timeout_ms is the between-pair budget; inference_timeout_ms is the hard per-request timeout; load_timeout_ms is separate.
Status is exposed through memory status and memory_repair semantic_control status.
Notices are advisory and can be listed/dismissed without governance authorization.
Section split is bound to vec readiness; there is no split.enabled toggle.
The original memory commits first. Safe Markdown-heading plans are queued to a background rule worker.
Unstructured/unsafe long documents return split_request for Agent-side continuation with the Agent's own LLM.
A zero section match returns the full memory.
